investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T03:52:18–21Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents, carrying the swarm error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every remote-agents check, the quota rejection prevented any agent from being provisioned, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) uncollected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard per-org remote agent quota of 100. At the time the eval ran, that quota was already at or above the limit, so every POST /api/agents call issued by the eval runner was rejected with HTTP 409 before an agent could be created. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition on the production-api swarm backend; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval targeting the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=1980) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 HTTP status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint resolved by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL was not reachable at eval time. The same check passed on the desktop-release runtime (latencyMs=137882, imageUrlPresent=true), confirming the image generation pipeline itself is functional and the failure is isolated to the production-api harness connectivity used by this eval.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api runtime harness endpoint was unreachable (HTTP 404) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream. The stream emitted a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED before any generation progress could occur, preventing the generation_completed frame and image artifact URL from ever being produced. This is an eval infrastructure connectivity failure scoped to the production-api runtime environment, not a confirmed user-facing outage. The check is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational for this runtime, which limits its blast radius to observability signal only.
proof: failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = [generation_start, generation_error, message]; generation_completed is absent; imageUrlPresent=false — both contract assertions violated.

sibling.image-generation-stream: the identical check on runtimeEnvironment=desktop-release passed with latencyMs=137882, frameTypes containing generation_completed, and imageUrlPresent=true — proving the image generation pipeline is operational and the failure is environment-specific.

possibleCauses: Primary: The agent runtime harness targeted by the production-api eval environment (resolved via LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL) was not deployed, was down, or returned 404 for the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint at the time of the eval run. This is the most direct reading of the SESSION_OPEN_FAILED / 404 error.

Secondary: The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable used by the production-api eval runner was misconfigured, pointed to a stale or wrong host, or was missing entirely, causing the request to resolve to an endpoint that does not serve this route.

Tertiary: The production-api harness was deployed at an incompatible version that does not expose /api/generate/image/stream or has changed its routing, as suggested by the error message text 'running an incompatible version'.

Lower confidence: A transient network or DNS issue caused a one-time 404 at eval time; the desktop-release sibling passing in the same run window makes a broad network outage less likely, but a production-api-specific routing or load-balancer issue remains possible.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T03:52:18–21Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents, carrying the swarm error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every remote-agents check, the quota rejection prevented any agent from being provisioned, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) uncollected.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard per-org remote agent quota of 100. At the time the eval ran, that quota was already at or above the limit, so every POST /api/agents call issued by the eval runner was rejected with HTTP 409 before an agent could be created. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition on the production-api swarm backend; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet.

possibleCauses: Most likely: the eval runner's org already has 100 remote swarm agents registered and the swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100, rejecting any new creation with HTTP 409. Prior eval runs or other automation may have created agents that were not cleaned up, accumulating against the quota.

Less likely but possible: a previous eval run crashed inside withCleanup before the cleanup callback could delete the probe agent, leaving a leaked agent that counts against the quota. Repeated leaks across runs would eventually exhaust the limit.

Least likely given identical messages across all three sibling checks: a transient swarm service error that happens to surface as a quota conflict; this would be disproved if a re-run succeeds without any agent deletion.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval targeting the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=1980) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 HTTP status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint resolved by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL was not reachable at eval time. The same check passed on the desktop-release runtime (latencyMs=137882, imageUrlPresent=true), confirming the image generation pipeline itself is functional and the failure is isolated to the production-api harness connectivity used by this eval.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api runtime harness endpoint was unreachable (HTTP 404) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream. The stream emitted a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED before any generation progress could occur, preventing the generation_completed frame and image artifact URL from ever being produced. This is an eval infrastructure connectivity failure scoped to the production-api runtime environment, not a confirmed user-facing outage. The check is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational for this runtime, which limits its blast radius to observability signal only.
proof: failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = [generation_start, generation_error, message]; generation_completed is absent; imageUrlPresent=false — both contract assertions violated.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1980 — the check failed in under 2 seconds, consistent with an immediate connection rejection rather than a timeout or slow generation failure.

sibling.image-generation-stream: the identical check on runtimeEnvironment=desktop-release passed with latencyMs=137882, frameTypes containing generation_completed, and imageUrlPresent=true — proving the image generation pipeline is operational and the failure is environment-specific.

possibleCauses: Primary: The agent runtime harness targeted by the production-api eval environment (resolved via LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL) was not deployed, was down, or returned 404 for the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint at the time of the eval run. This is the most direct reading of the SESSION_OPEN_FAILED / 404 error.

Secondary: The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable used by the production-api eval runner was misconfigured, pointed to a stale or wrong host, or was missing entirely, causing the request to resolve to an endpoint that does not serve this route.

Tertiary: The production-api harness was deployed at an incompatible version that does not expose /api/generate/image/stream or has changed its routing, as suggested by the error message text 'running an incompatible version'.

Lower confidence: A transient network or DNS issue caused a one-time 404 at eval time; the desktop-release sibling passing in the same run window makes a broad network outage less likely, but a production-api-specific routing or load-balancer issue remains possible.
